title: AI debt collection platform CreditNirvana exposed about 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings
date_note: Published November 18; the flaws were reported May 30 and fixed June 2, 2026.
summary: Researcher Eaton Zveare reported two flaws in the CreditNirvana collections platform: a hardcoded API key in the AI call centre and a login bypass in the main platform. They exposed about 6.6 million accounts and about 315,000 call recordings. Both were fixed on June 2, 2026.
plain: Two security holes in an AI debt-collection service made millions of borrowers' records and call recordings reachable without a proper login. They were fixed in June.
exec: Shows third-party AI collections platforms can expose lenders' customer data at scale; lenders using them inherit the risk.
action: If you run CreditNirvana, confirm the call centre is on 2.0.0 and the collections platform on 4.8.2, per CERT-In; lenders should review vendor access controls.
impact: About 6.6 million accounts and about 315,000 call recordings accessible.

validation.note: eaton-works.com (the researcher's own write-up) and receivablesinfo.com (relaying Wired and the CERT-In advisory) agree on numbers, CVEs and the June 2 fix; Receivables Info says CreditNirvana and Perfios did not respond to WIRED. Wired itself was not read.

review.note: unsourced absence: removed 'Nothing shows attackers used them'; added evidence quotes, source published days, validation note; figures, CVEs, dates match

evidence.quote: approximately 315,000 recorded collection calls, transcripts, and AI-generated recommendations
